title: 10/7/2026 | Mark D Owens | COM | Public comments on data centers, 765 kV, and the Governor’s audit. Specifically near La Grange, Tx

documents.text:
=== PUCT Impact Statement for Data Center.pdf ===
My wife and I retired to Winchester area near La Grange, Texas because we believed we had
finally found a place where we could enjoy the peace, quiet, open land, and wildlife that are
becoming increasingly difficult to find. After 25 years working in the computer software
industry, I retired only weeks ago. We invested a substantial portion of our retirement savings to
purchase property near La Grange and have already begun building the home where we
intended to spend our retirement.

Now, before we have even finished building that home, we are facing the possibility of a
massive data center being developed less than two miles from our property.

This is not a minor development that will have a limited effect on a few nearby landowners. A
data center of this size has the potential to permanently change the character of our
community and directly affect the people who already live here.

We are asking the Public Utility Commission of Texas to ensure that the residents and
landowners who will be directly affected are fully informed and given a meaningful opportunity
to participate before decisions are made that could permanently alter our community.



We are deeply concerned about what this development could mean for the quality of life we
worked and saved for. A facility of this size could bring significant construction traffic,
permanent increases in traffic, noise and light pollution, and disruption to the wildlife and rural
character of the area. It could also affect neighboring ranches, livestock, and the people who
have chosen to live in Winchester precisely because of its quiet, rural environment.

Water is another serious concern. We need to understand how much water this facility will
require, where that water will come from, and what impact that demand could have on existing
landowners and groundwater resources. We are now questioning whether it is even safe to
proceed with our own well without knowing how this project could affect the area's water
supply. Another concern about water is the waste water from the data center. How much waste
water will there be, where is it expect to go?

We are also concerned about the potential impact on electricity costs and the local electric grid.
A data center of this magnitude represents an extraordinary demand for power, and local
residents should not be left wondering whether they will ultimately bear increased costs or
experience impacts to the reliability of their electric service.

Winchester is a small, close-knit community. It is a place where people value their neighbors,
their land, their livestock, the wildlife, and the peace and quiet that have defined this area for
generations. We did not invest our retirement savings and begin building our home here
expecting to live next to a massive industrial development.
 We recognize that companies have rights to purchase property and develop it in accordance
with applicable laws and regulations. However, those rights do not exist in isolation.

Nearby landowners also have legitimate rights and interests that deserve consideration—
including the right to protect the use and enjoyment of their homes, property, water resources,
and established way of life.

We did not purchase our property with the expectation that we would eventually be living next
to a massive industrial facility. We made a significant financial and personal commitment based
on the rural character of this community. For us, this is not an abstract development proposal.
This is the place where we planned to spend the rest of our lives.

If a project of this magnitude is going to fundamentally change the environment surrounding
existing homes and ranches, the people who will live with those consequences deserve more
than limited information after decisions have already been made.

They deserve transparency before decisions are finalized, meaningful public participation, and
a thorough examination of the project's full costs and impacts.

My wife and I worked for decades and used a substantial portion of our retirement savings to
build what we believed would be our peaceful home. We are not asking for special treatment.
We are asking for transparency, accountability, and the opportunity for our community to
understand and participate in decisions that could permanently change the place we call home.

The people who live here should have a meaningful voice in determining what happens to our
community.
